record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own training NLL and Hessian results for ViTs and CNNs, including conditions where ViT training is hindered and where those effects improve. This refines the broad claim by showing architecture, dataset size, inductive bias, and augmentation matter; it does not measure classification training error directly.
record.gate_note: Training NLL and loss curvature are reported for the paper's own models; related to optimization but not the training classification-error measure in V1. Results about architecture and non-convex losses bear on the broad claim and V3. Cited results from prior work are not rows. The paper does not report initialization comparisons, learning-rate stability sweeps, or batch-normalization comparisons.
record.test_reason: The study measures architecture-dependent training NLL, test performance and loss curvature, but none of V1–V6. It does not measure training classification error, depth degradation with and without identity shortcuts, initialization effects, teacher–student local-minimum frequencies, learning-rate stability thresholds, or normalization effects. Comparing ViTs with ResNets does not test V3.
record.authors_conclusion: The record captures the authors' optimization interpretation, but its no-overfitting statement needs the tested strong-augmentation setting. The authors attribute poor small-data ViT performance to optimization difficulty rather than overfitting, and argue that more data, appropriate locality and smoothing methods help. Their broader conclusion is that MSAs act as spatial smoothings complementary to convolutions, motivating AlterNet. The curvature-based causal explanation is the authors' interpretation.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains vision architectures from scratch with AdamW and strong DeiT-style augmentation, and measures training NLL, test error, and Hessian curvature; it does not use the versions' stated training-error protocols.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with dataset size, architecture and inductive bias, local MSA kernel size, patch size, number of heads, embedding dimensions per head, training duration, classifier (CLS versus GAP), and augmentation strength.

fits_no_version.finding: Under the tested augmentation recipe, ViTs have worse training NLL and test performance than CNNs on small datasets; reducing dataset size worsens both, while longer training improves both.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Architecture, dataset size and training duration affect optimization of augmented-data NLL in vision models.

fits_no_version.finding: Attention locality and patch size affect training NLL and test performance; GAP improves accuracy by 2.7 percentage points and suppresses negative sampled Hessian eigenvalues.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Specific architectural biases can improve ViT loss optimization and predictive performance.

fits_no_version.finding: ViTs and ResNets differ in sampled Hessian eigenvalues; more heads and larger embedding dimensions reduce the reported non-convexity and sharpness metrics.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Vision architecture and attention dimensions affect sampled local loss curvature.

fits_no_version.finding: Larger models explore lower NLL regions and have smaller sampled Hessian eigenvalues early in training; large ViTs have flatter minima late in training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Model size affects NLL landscapes and local curvature in the tested vision models.

fits_no_version.finding: Strong augmentation reduces sampled Hessian eigenvalue magnitudes while producing more negative eigenvalues; the authors interpret this as hindering convergence to low training loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Strong augmentation can flatten local loss curvature while increasing measured non-convexity.

record.problems: The relevant optimization evidence is mainly training NLL and Hessian-curvature proxies, not training classification error. Many plotted comparisons lack exact numerical values in the text; no uncertainty estimates are stated. Models use strong data augmentation and regularization, so the results do not isolate unregularized training.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Cited findings from earlier papers are not extracted as this study's own results.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training classification error in sufficiently large CNNs, including random or corrupted labels, and its dependence on model size, stopping and regularization. Augmented-data NLL does not establish classification training error.
Two-layer ReLU teacher–student optimization, spurious-local-minimum frequencies, and the effect of one or two extra student neurons.
Depth-dependent training degradation in plain batch-normalized CNNs, prevention by identity shortcuts, and the special-initialization exceptions.
Activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization, training speed and trainable depth.
Recovery above the initial stability limit, curvature reduction during a loss spike, edge-of-stability dynamics and divergence relative to the threshold.
Training speed and learning-rate tolerance with versus without batch normalization, and Fixup's normalization-free alternative.

record.verdict_notes: Remove all three recorded V3 verdicts. Neither related optimization results nor curvature proxies justify extending V3 to arbitrary architecture comparisons. All row states are cannot_determine relative to the listed versions; this does not negate the reported NLL or curvature trends. No omitted result in the supplied text directly tests V1–V6.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, random or corrupted labels, and comparisons among model sizes, early stopping, and regularized recipes.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious minima frequency, and student width relative to teacher width.

Plain versus residual matched-depth training error comparisons and explicit tests of identity shortcuts. The paper compares different architectures and reports NLL and curvature, not classification training error.
Initialization choices and their effect on speed or trainable depth.
Learning rates above stability limits, loss recovery, sharpness hovering at a threshold, and divergence.
Batch normalization versus no normalization and Fixup training.

rows.subject: ResNet
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR-100; training NLL and test error reported across model comparison.
rows.value: Figure 5a; exact values not stated in text.
rows.note: The figure gives model-specific results, but the supplied text does not state exact ResNet values. This measures NLL, not training classification error.
rows.check: ResNet training NLL and test error do not establish depth degradation or the effect of identity shortcuts. Training NLL is measured on augmented training data.

rows.subject: ViT
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR-100; training NLL and test error reported across model comparison.
rows.value: Figure 5a; exact values not stated in text.
rows.note: The authors state weak-inductive-bias ViTs have inferior training NLL to CNNs in small-data regimes. NLL is not classification training error.
rows.check: Inferior ViT training NLL relative to CNNs does not test V3; architecture differs without a controlled depth or shortcut comparison.

rows.subject: ViT
rows.operation_detail: Training duration varied on CIFAR; training NLL and test error reported.
rows.value: Both training NLL and test error decrease as epochs increase; exact values not stated in text.
rows.note: The authors say ViT predictive performance remains inferior to ResNet across epoch counts. This is not a direct training classification-error measure.
rows.check: Longer training reduces NLL and test error, but there is no comparison of plain versus residual networks or depth degradation. Figure C.3 includes both ViT and ResNet; its caption identifies CIFAR without specifying CIFAR-100.

rows.subject: ViT with convolutional MSAs
rows.operation_detail: Kernel size of local convolutional MSA varied; training NLL and test error measured.
rows.value: 5 × 5 outperforms 8 × 8 on both training and test datasets; 3 × 3 NLL is worse than 5 × 5 but better than global MSA.
rows.note: Explicit comparison of training NLL by locality; does not measure classification training error.
rows.check: Changing attention locality measures a different architectural intervention from V3. The qualitative NLL comparisons are supported.

rows.subject: ViT with GAP classifier
rows.operation_detail: Replaced CLS-token classifier with global average pooling and measured accuracy change and Hessian spectrum.
rows.measure: test accuracy change and Hessian negative eigenvalues
rows.baseline: ViT with CLS token; exact accuracy not stated
rows.value: +2.7 percent point; GAP suppresses negative Hessian max eigenvalues
rows.note: Optimization-related evidence only; accuracy improvement does not establish training classification error.
rows.check: The GAP versus CLS comparison reports accuracy and curvature, without testing depth degradation, identity shortcuts or another listed version.

rows.subject: ViT with local MSA
rows.operation_detail: Compared locality conditions using negative Hessian eigenvalues and training NLL.
rows.measure: negative Hessian eigenvalues and training NLL
rows.value: 5 × 5 has fewer negative eigenvalues than global MSA and 3 × 3; 3 × 3 training NLL is between 5 × 5 and global MSA.
rows.note: The result shows locality changes the reported optimization indicators; not classification training error.
rows.check: Locality-dependent curvature and NLL do not test V3. The NLL component duplicates R4; separate the curvature result if retaining both rows.

rows.subject: ViT
rows.operation_detail: Training dataset size varied and training NLL and test error measured.
rows.baseline: full dataset, exact values not stated
rows.value: As dataset size decreases, error increases and training NLL also increases; with strong augmentation, authors report no overfitting at 2% dataset size.
rows.note: Training NLL worsens as data decreases, but the authors specifically characterize this as optimization difficulty rather than overfitting.
rows.check: Dataset-size effects on ViT training NLL do not test any listed version. The no-overfitting interpretation applies to the strong-augmentation recipe and augmented-data NLL.

rows.subject: ViT
rows.operation_detail: Measured Hessian eigenvalue spectrum during training against ResNet.

conditions.value: early phase; later at 100th, 200th, and 300th epochs

rows.measure: Hessian eigenvalue spectrum, including negative eigenvalues
rows.baseline: ResNet has only a few negative eigenvalues
rows.value: ViT has a number of negative Hessian eigenvalues; its positive eigenvalue magnitudes are smaller than ResNet's.
rows.note: Curvature proxy for non-convex optimization, not training classification error.
rows.check: Hessian spectra are not a measure of V3's depth-dependent training error. These are distributions of top-five eigenvalues computed on minibatches, not a full Hessian spectrum; the prominent negative-eigenvalue comparison concerns early training.

rows.subject: ViT
rows.operation_detail: Embedding patch size varied; training NLL and Hessian spectra measured.
rows.measure: training NLL, test error, and Hessian spectrum
rows.value: Both large and small patch sizes harm performance; small patch size produces negative eigenvalues while reducing eigenvalue magnitudes.
rows.note: The text states the direction of the effects but not exact training NLL values.
rows.check: Patch-size effects on NLL, test error and curvature do not test any listed version.

rows.subject: ViT
rows.operation_detail: Number of attention heads varied and loss curvature summarized by NEP and APE.
rows.measure: negative eigenvalue proportion (NEP) and average positive eigenvalues (APE)
rows.value: Both NEP and APE decrease as the number of heads increases.
rows.note: Curvature metrics rather than classification training error; the text gives no individual numbers.
rows.check: Attention-head effects on curvature do not measure V2's teacher–student spurious-minimum frequency or V3. NEP and APE concern sampled top eigenvalues. The experiment uses a ViT with half the usual depth.

rows.subject: ViT
rows.operation_detail: Embedding dimensions per head varied and loss curvature summarized by NEP and APE.
rows.measure: negative eigenvalue proportion (NEP) and average positive eigenvalues (APE)
rows.value: Both NEP and APE decrease as embedding dimensions per head increase.
rows.note: Curvature metrics rather than classification training error.
rows.check: Embedding-dimension effects on curvature do not test any listed version. NEP and APE concern sampled top eigenvalues. The experiment uses a ViT with half the usual depth.

rows.subject: ViT
rows.operation_detail: Model size compared using loss landscapes and Hessian eigenvalue spectra.
rows.measure: training NLL landscape and Hessian eigenvalues
rows.value: Large models explore low NLLs; their Hessian eigenvalues are smaller than those of small models early in training; large ViTs have flat minima late in training.
rows.note: The reported comparison concerns NLL and local curvature, not classification training error.
rows.check: Model-size comparisons of NLL landscapes and curvature do not establish near-zero training classification error or depth degradation. Figure C.7 also includes ResNet-50 and ResNet-101, which should be separate subjects if extracted.

rows.subject: ViT with strong data augmentation
rows.operation_detail: Compared strong augmentation with weak augmentation and measured Hessian spectrum.

conditions.value: strong DeiT-style versus weak resize and crop

rows.value: Strong augmentation reduces eigenvalue magnitudes and produces a lot of negative Hessian eigenvalues; authors say this prevents convergence to low training losses.
rows.note: This is a stated limitation under the study's augmentation comparison, using loss curvature and training loss rather than training classification error.
rows.check: Augmentation-dependent curvature and the authors' interpretation about training loss do not test V3. Figure F.1b reports sampled top Hessian eigenvalues; it does not directly quantify the claimed failure to converge to low loss.

rows.subject: ResNet
rows.operation_detail: Compared strong augmentation with weak augmentation and measured Hessian spectrum.

conditions.value: strong DeiT-style versus weak resize and crop

rows.value: Strong augmentation reduces eigenvalue magnitudes and produces a lot of negative Hessian eigenvalues.
rows.note: The figure reports the comparison but exact values are not stated in the text.

reader_labels.condition: ViT versus CNN optimization on small-data CIFAR settings
reader_labels.reason: ViT has non-convex losses and inferior training NLL to CNNs in small-data regimes, while the reported outcomes depend on architecture and inductive bias (R2, R4, R6, R7, R8). The study does not test the version's matched-depth shortcut claim.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: ViT training with more epochs and selected loss-smoothing or locality changes
reader_labels.reason: Training NLL decreases over longer training and selected architecture changes improve reported optimization indicators (R3, R5, R6).
